note: zzip_mem_entry_new() (zzip/memdisk.c) trusts the zip64 "largefile" extra-block pointer returned by zzip_mem_entry_extra_block() to be a full 40-byte struct zzip_extra_zip64 once it is merely non-null -- the finder only matches on the block's 2-byte datatype code, never on whether the block's own declared datasize actually covers the struct being overlaid. block->z_diskstart is then read via ZZIP_GET32 32 bytes into that struct; when the matched block sits near the tail of the heap-allocated extra-data copy (the same finder function scans forward with no bound on how far it walks), this read runs past the end of the allocation -- a heap-based out-of-bounds read.

traces.message: zzip_mem_entry_extra_block(item, ZZIP_EXTRA_zip64) : returns a block matched purely on its 2-byte datatype code, with no check that its declared datasize covers struct zzip_extra_zip64
if (block) : bare non-null guard, no size validation
item->zz_diskstart = ZZIP_GET32(block->z_diskstart) : reads 4 bytes 32 bytes into the (possibly truncated) block -- heap-based out-of-bounds read
